correctness.rationale: PASS: Over Watson–Crick four-letter alphabet, the reverse-complement involution on 256 four-mers has 136 orbits including 16 fixed words. Imposing all self/cross prefix–suffix nonoverlap lengths 1..3 and pairwise aligned Hamming distance≥2 leaves 56 individually valid orbits (12 singleton,44 doubleton). Their exact compatibility graph has 420 edges; RC-closed codebooks biject to its weighted cliques. The strictly decreasing exclusion/inclusion recursion F(S)=F(S\{v})+z^{s(v)}F((S\{v})∩N(v)) gives H(z)=(1,12,88,288,584,760,688,424,160,32), total 3037 and maximum 9 with 32 maximizers; the complement-preserving relabeling group has order 8 and acts in four full orbits, 24/8 structural split. Independent code rebuilt the graph and exact clique polynomial (1318 memo states), matching all ten coefficients. Source direct-word backtracker additionally verifies orbit classes. The finite exhaustive recursion proves exactly length 4, not arbitrary lengths.

value.rationale: PASS: A natural DNA barcode/synchronizing-code design conflict combines Watson–Crick reversal symmetry, strict frame nonoverlap and single-substitution detection. The complete four-mer cardinality polynomial and symmetries give an exact small-block feasibility benchmark and all optimal codebooks; the finite scope is inherent and mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary isolated integer.

limitations: Only length-four Watson–Crick alphabet; reverse-complement-fixed codewords allowed; Hamming≥2 detects but need not correct a substitution; no GC, thermodynamic or self-RC separation assumptions.
